stage1.impression: A moody, warm night interior with believable timber beams, a decent sense of depth and some atmosphere, but it reads as a competent CG render, not a photograph. The concrete floor carries hard stool shadows and blotchy stains under a hot pool that is brighter than anything at the far end. The zinc counter glows almost white, the Orbs are neutral white balls, and the 'hero' speakers are two tiny, flat, washed-white rectangles at the back that look pasted in and carry no tint. Repeated identical stools, chairs and Orbs give it a catalogue feel. As it stands a magazine would read this as a generic wood-and-concrete bar, not a specific place: the altar, the one thing that makes it Planet EARF, barely registers.

blocking_9: The altar pair must read as the hero at a glance: at least about 4% of the frame, with the smoked tint and the light through the acrylic visible, and no flat white faces (the left altar speaker currently measures median 61, p95 234, neutral R64 G60 B63)
The brightest broad surfaces must be the altar and the bar top's pools, not the foreground floor (floor [150,600,500,800] median 92 vs altar room [420,280,820,500] median 22)
The zinc counter must read as dark patinated metal with a pool on it, not a near-white strip (median 149, p95 241)
The Orbs must show their smoked tint around a frosted glow, not read as plain white spheres (median 179, near neutral)
No crushed foreground: the banquette [880,450,1200,800] crush_pct must be under 3 (now 7.2)
Visible signs of life and variety in the foreground (a coat or a record on the near chairs and tables); the repeated identical seats and Orbs read as instancing
Concrete and the floor must show formwork and pour detail at 1:1, not flat blotchy texture

defects.what: Left altar speaker reads as a flat white card with a blown batt face, no smoked tint and no acrylic depth
Right altar speaker is the same: a flat white face, half cut by the doorway jamb, and it looks composited
The spot cones in the haze are visible as hard grey wedges above the speakers and read as CG volumetrics
The foreground floor is a hot cool-grey pool (median 92) with hard-edged stool shadows and blotchy stains that read as a decal texture
The zinc counter top is near-white (median 149, p95 241) and reads as a glowing slab, not a metal top
The front Orb is a pure white sphere (median 179, R183 G177 B163) with no visible tint; all the Orbs in the row are identical
The banquette and the right foreground fall into crush (median 19.8, crush 7.2%)
The framed screens show blurred grey-violet images that read as out-of-focus placeholders, and their cool cast fights the warm room
The concrete wall reads flat and olive with sparse speckles, with no board grain, tie holes or pour lines visible
Repeated identical stools and chairs in a perfect line read as instanced geometry
The back-bar speaker reads as a grey, untinted panel, washed by the lit niche strip

changes.problem: The hero pair fills well under 1% of the frame at the end of a long tunnel, so the eye lands on the floor and the counter instead.

evidence.measured: The two altar speakers are each about 40 x 75 px in a 1200 x 800 frame; the right one is clipped by the doorway jamb.

change.to: position [3.2, 2.4, 1.30], target [16.5, 3.05, 1.15] (centred on the altar so both speakers clear the jambs), 40 mm, f/4 focused at [16.0, 3.05, 1.1]

changes.expected: The altar pair roughly doubles in height (about 150 px at this scale) and sits centred in the doorway, with the counter and banquette still framing it left and right. The far room stays sharp and the foreground stools soften slightly.

changes.problem: The 300 W, 22 degree altar spots blow the white batts so each speaker reads as a flat white card, while the cabinet tint and the altar around it stay dark.

evidence.measured: Median 61, p95 234, range 216, neutral R64 G60 B63: a hot face on a dark surround with no tint

change.to: 160 W, 2700 K, cone 36 deg, aimed 0.3 m above the cabinet's top so the beam grazes down the acrylic and spills onto the altar and the back wall

changes.expected: The cabinets read as tinted smoked acrylic with lit edges and a softer batt glow, and the altar and the wall behind them lift out of black.

changes.problem: The Dome downlights throw a hot, hard pool on the foreground floor that outshines the hero and draws hard CG stool shadows.

evidence.measured: Median 92, p95 194, cool-grey R103 G90 B79, against the altar room's median 22

change.setting: lamps: the Domes' downlights 4 x spot
change.to: 22 W, 2400 K, cone 24 deg, with a spot radius (soft size) of 0.06 m so the shadows soften

changes.expected: The floor sinks to a warm mid-dark with soft-edged pools under the counter. The counter top keeps its pool, and the eye travels to the far end.

changes.problem: The zinc counter top reads as a near-white glowing slab, not patinated metal.

change.to: dark aged zinc: base colour about #5E5C58, roughness 0.45 with mottled variation of 0.35 to 0.6, so the downlight reads as a soft pool with a sheen

changes.expected: The counter reads as grey-brown metal with a soft highlight under each Dome, darker than the pendants themselves.

changes.problem: The Orbs read as plain white balls, so the smoked tint (the products' colour) is lost and they look like stock globe lamps.

evidence.measured: Median 179, R183 G177 B163, near neutral

change.to: 0.10 W, glow 0.0045, and frosted liner roughness up from the current value to 0.85 so the tinted shell reads around a softer core

changes.expected: Each Orb shows a smoky darker rim around a warm frosted core and a small pool on its table top.

changes.problem: The banquette and the right foreground crush, so the room's most inviting seating is a black mass.

change.setting: the screens' images, plus one practical
change.from: screens 0.035, no light on the banquette back
change.to: screens 0.02 (and a warmer grade), plus a candle on the nearest banquette table (one of the 2 candles moved from the counter, 3 W, 1900 K)

changes.expected: The banquette's leather and fluting hold detail in a low warm glow, and the screens stop reading as cool placeholders.

changes.problem: The foreground is empty and identical seats repeat in a perfect line, which reads as a showroom or instancing, not a lived-in bar.

evidence.measured: Seen: six identical counter stools at equal spacing, four identical chairs and four identical Orbs in a row, and only one glass in the foreground

change.from: round 39 props: 3 rocks, 2 coupes, 5 napkins, 2 votives, 1 matchbook, 1 coat (mostly at the counter and the zone)
change.to: move the coat to the nearest chair at about [470,600-760], add a record and its sleeve leaning on the nearest table, add a half-drunk rocks glass and a napkin on the second table, and rotate three of the stools and two chairs by 5 to 15 degrees

changes.expected: The near third reads as a room moments after people stood up. The rhythm breaks so nothing reads as an array.

changes.problem: The board-formed concrete and the floor read flat and blotchy, with none of the formwork grain, tie holes or pour lines that make the material real at 1:1.

evidence.measured: Median 78, range 95 with a smooth olive field (R92 G75 B67) and only scattered speckles; the floor stains repeat as decal-like blotches

change.setting: the concrete's tone and sheen; the floor's polish
change.from: flat olive tone, matte; floor with high-contrast blotches
change.to: a warmer neutral grey (about #8A847C under 2700 K), with the board-grain bump raised so the 150 mm boards and tie holes read, roughness 0.8; floor polish to roughness 0.35 and the stain map's contrast halved

changes.expected: The wall shows boards and pour lines in the raking Orb and spot light, and the floor shows soft, blurred reflections of the pools instead of stains.

out_of_scope.request: Give the speakers' Smoke tint more saturation so they carry the frame's colour
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' colour and parts are fixed. Only the light on them (c2) and the camera (c1) may change.

out_of_scope.request: Widen or move the doorway to the listening room so the right altar speaker isn't cut by the jamb
out_of_scope.why: The room's layout is fixed. c1 addresses this through the camera instead.

out_of_scope.request: Vary the seat models so they don't all match
out_of_scope.why: The seats are part of the fixed design. Only their placement and props may change (c7).
